narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Mostly cloudy skies will turn partly cloudy by midday with winds from the SSW, becoming overcast in the evening. High of 29°C (84°F) and low of 19°C (66°F). Showers & Thunderstorms Likely with 10.4 mm (0.41 in) of rain expected starting From 17:00. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Peak gusts will reach 38 km/h (21 kt). The UV index will peak at 9.2 today. Air quality is at AQI 57. As of 06:01, reports through 03:30: no rain; no thunder; high so far 18°C (64°F); low so far 18°C (64°F); peak sustained 4 km/h (2 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

Cooling through Thursday, with rain and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies mostly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday, then overcast Thursday. Thursday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs around 25°C (77°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 86 checks.

Further out, warming through Monday, with rain and thunderstorms possible Friday, showers and thunderstorms likely Saturday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Sunday and Monday. Friday: all four models wet, highs 19 to 24°C (66 to 76°F), thunder possible rather than likely. Saturday: all four models wet, highs 24 to 27°C (75 to 80°F), thunder likely rather than possible. Sunday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 27°C (81°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Saturday. UKMO is the wetter solution from Friday to Saturday; GFS, ECMWF and ICON keep it drier. Monday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 27°C (81°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 82 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability in the hours ahead: UKMO 3860 J/kg, ECMWF 1740 J/kg, ICON 1300 J/kg and GFS 910 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 38 km/h (21 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 29 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the west (1013 hPa) and highest toward the southwest (1016 hPa) — a 3 hPa spread, a weak large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the east, north, south, southeast — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1016.0 and 1018.0 hPa, falling by 2.1 hPa over three days. Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -1.5 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ECMWF first at Day+3, right 87% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 90% of the last 30 checks. On today's high GFS is the warmest model at 30.1°C (86.2°F) and ECMWF the coolest at 27.8°C (82.0°F); the call's 29.0°C (84.2°F) sits between them. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs here.

Today's Forecast by Gemini 3.6 Flash; the rest written by code.
